safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no specific area of tenderness.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not document 'no specific area of tenderness'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the negative finding of no focal tenderness in a knee pain history slightly reduces documentation quality but is unlikely to change immediate management (still requires exam/physio assessment). This is low-risk compared with medication/allergy or red-flag symptom errors.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies other joint pains and denies feeling generally unwell or febrile.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document denial of other joint pains and systemic symptoms (fever/unwell) can blur screening for inflammatory or infectious etiologies and may lead to unnecessary escalation or missed reassurance. While the overall presentation remains consistent with an overuse injury, omission of fever/systemic negatives carries some clinical relevance.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither gold nor transcript states a morphine allergy/adverse reaction; transcript only notes GP advised ER not to give morphine.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly labeling morphine as an allergy/adverse reaction can meaningfully affect future acute pain management, causing avoidance of first-line opioids and substitution with less effective or higher-risk alternatives. In urgent settings this can lead to undertreated pain and potentially more complex medication choices.
